extraction.title: Buttonwood
extraction.subtitle: Can Bill Ackman save the closed-end fund? An outspoken financier wants to build a modern-day Berkshire Hathaway
extraction.summary: Bill Ackman raised $5 bn to launch Pershing Square USA, the largest US‑listed closed‑end fund, hoping to overcome chronic NAV discounts that plague the asset class. By listing domestically and retaining a large manager stake, he seeks to attract stable capital and replicate the outperformance of his earlier Pershing Square Holdings, while recent activist activity (Saba Capital vs. Edinburgh Worldwide) underscores the risks of discount‑driven takeovers.

narratives.name: Reviving the closed‑end fund model
narratives.thesis: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square USA aims to eliminate persistent NAV discounts by leveraging a domestic listing, large manager stake, and strong branding, potentially restoring investor confidence in closed‑end funds.

narratives.name: NAV discount as a market inefficiency
narratives.thesis: Long‑standing discounts to NAV in closed‑end funds create arbitrage opportunities and attract activist takeovers, reflecting structural frictions rather than manager performance.
